context.guidance: For a Third Schedule class, send the Data Principal a notice at least 48 hours before erasure under Rule 8(2), telling them the erasure is due and how to stop it. Build the notice into the erasure job so that it always runs ahead of deletion and cannot be skipped. Apply the requirement only where the Third Schedule class condition is met, not by default.

value.fix: Don't delete straight away from this handler. Have it record a scheduled erasure that a single erasure job carries out, and build the Rule 8(2) notice into that job only when the Third Schedule class condition is met. (1) Add fields to PrivacyRequestModel: thirdScheduleClass (boolean), noticeSentAt, scheduledErasureAt, cancelledAt and status (pending_notice | notified | cancelled | erased). (2) In the POST handler, create the request with deletionRequested: true, and set thirdScheduleClass by calling a central helper such as isThirdScheduleClass(dataFiduciary, purpose). Base that helper on config for the entity class (e-commerce, online gaming or social media intermediary over the user threshold) and the purpose. Don't hard-code it to true. Set status to 'pending_notice' if the condition is met. Otherwise follow the existing erasure path unchanged, so the 48-hour notice isn't applied by default. (3) In the erasure job, for Third Schedule records: if noticeSentAt is null, send the Data Principal a notice (email or registered contact) saying their personal data will be erased on scheduledErasureAt, and explaining how to stop it, for example by logging in, using the account, or a cancel link or endpoint. Save noticeSentAt, set scheduledErasureAt to at least noticeSentAt + 48 hours, set status to 'notified', and don't delete anything in that run. Delete only when status is 'notified', noticeSentAt is set, now >= noticeSentAt + 48h, and cancelledAt is null. Check this inside the delete function itself, so no other code path can skip the notice. If sending the notice fails, keep the record pending and retry, and never fall through to deletion. (4) Add a cancel route (for example POST /erasure/cancel/:id, authenticated or with a signed token) that sets cancelledAt and status 'cancelled'. Also treat any login or activity by the Data Principal before scheduledErasureAt as cancelling the erasure. (5) Keep an audit log of the notice's content, when it was sent, the delivery channel, and the erasure or cancellation outcome. (6) Add tests: Third Schedule records are never erased without a notice sent at least 48h earlier; a cancellation stops erasure; non-Third Schedule records follow the normal flow with no notice gate.
